_readme: These are MEASURED baselines, not targets. Each number here was captured by actually
running the named command and reading its output on the date recorded in the entry's
Changing any number in this file is a deliberate act that belongs in the SAME commit as
whatever changed the underlying measurement (a fix, a new test, a dependency bump). This
file is never edited to make a red CI run go green without that accompanying change.
A DROP in a failure count is as much a reason to investigate as a RISE. A failure that
disappeared without a commit that fixed it is a signal, not a free pass — see voteEngine's
exact (not floor) check on both count and titles.
scripts/assert-ci-baselines.mjs reads this file by import.meta.url, never mutates it, and
has no 'update the baseline' mode. Updating a baseline is a human, reviewed commit.

voteEngine.note: Human shorthand for the 8 verbatim titles above, in order: InsertOnly x2 (AuthorityEngine InviteSlot + AdminSigning), a CID probe (D-01 compat gate Probe 3b), cadre-core clusterSize (post-peerId-patch blocker 2), Optimystic composite-PK x2 (DELETE storage-key bug + its single-column control), P2P-11 residual x2 (findCluster addressless-seeding blocker + its installed-version tripwire). All 8 are pre-existing and unchanged across this phase. minPassing was re-measured live during 50-13 at 1411 (up from an earlier phase-history figure of 1356 recorded before this wave's plans landed additional passing tests) — see the 50-13 SUMMARY's Deviations section. ciMinPassing is deliberately one LOWER than minPassing, not a copy-paste slip: `.planning/` is a nested git repo the outer repo gitignores (zero tracked files in the outer tree), so a fresh CI checkout never has it. `test/strand-cohort-routing-coverage.spec.ts`'s 'the diagnosis doc is present...' test now guards on `existsSync(.planning/...)` and calls `this.skip()` when absent, so on CI it reports as one of the pending tests instead of a passing one -- visibly, not silently. expectedFailing stays exactly 8 in BOTH environments; only the passing/pending split moves. The checker's `vote-engine` subcommand takes an explicit `--ci` flag (the workflow always passes it) and picks ciMinPassing over minPassing when set, rather than sniffing a CI env var, so the choice is visible in the workflow file and reproducible outside it.

dashboardTier1.note: 50-04's original local budget was 5s at 12 tests. The suite has grown to 326 tests across 50-05/50-08/50-09/50-12, and a live re-run during 50-13 measured ~17.5s internal / ~18s wall on this machine three times in a row. maxSeconds was therefore set to 45 (not the phase-history figure of 15, which is now stale and would fail on a clean run before any CI slowness is even added) to give real CI headroom over the current measured cost. The bound exists to keep tier 1 a fast gate -- exceeding it is a signal the tier is drifting into something else, not a number to raise reflexively. See the 50-13 SUMMARY's Deviations section for the full measurement. Raised 326 -> 330 by the code-review fix for CR-01, which added four assertions to test/node/preview-control.test.mjs (the re-seed matcher, its inertness control, the dead-prop matcher and its inertness control) -- re-measured live at 330 pass / 0 fail / ~19.5s in the same commit that added them. Raised 330 -> 332 by the fix for WR-02, which added a copyKeyForPhase totality test and its unmapped-phase control, then 332 -> 334 by WR-04 (the relabelled-envelope refusal and its clean-bootstrap positive control) 334 -> 335 by WR-05 (the blocked-delete record-survival test) 335 -> 337 by WR-06 (the non-creating listObjectStores probe and its present-database positive control) and 337 -> 341 by WR-10 (the new test/node/shell-wiring.test.mjs source suite, two matchers plus two inertness controls), then 341 -> 344 by WR-11 (the handle-handover matcher, its close-after inertness control and the both-call-sites check), then 344 -> 347 by WR-12 (panel console hygiene, its inertness control and the nine-site count) and 347 -> 350 by WR-16 (the banner-default matcher, its old-shape inertness control and the distinct-copy check) 350 -> 351 by WR-17 (the applied-count test) and 351 -> 355 by WR-18 (the empty-expected-name refusal, its non-empty positive control, and the shell-side guard plus its inertness control). Raised 355 -> 364 by 50-14 Task 1's CR-01 gap closure: 9 new `resyncRealScopes` cases in test/node/preview-scopes.test.mjs (referential stability, the CR-01 empty-to-nine transition, the sticky touched guard plus its positive control, order-insensitivity, duplicates, validation parity, and the frozen/no-mutation check) -- re-measured live at 364 pass / 0 fail / ~18-19s wall in the same commit range that added them. preview-control.test.mjs's existing assertions were updated in place (not added), so its count is unchanged. Raised 364 -> 370 by 50-16's gap-closure plan: Task 1 added 5 new refresh-swap.test.mjs cases proving the CR-02 repair path (an explicit-empty-counts variant of the row-count record, a genuine post-swap divergence, the unheld-network throw, a storage-sequence-log proof of read-after-write with zero extra writes, and a direct write-count assertion on a verify-failed refusal), and Task 2's copy.test.mjs rewrite net +1 (two copyKeyForPhase tests replaced by three: the mechanical bootstrap.phase.<value> coverage test, its unmapped-key throw, and a new panelFrame.*Pill interpolation test) -- re-measured live at 370 pass / 0 fail / ~19.8s wall in the same commit range that added them.

authorityTypecheck.note: This is a ceiling, not a floor: the producer half added to apps/VoteTorrentAuthority by this phase must introduce none. A drop below 51 means someone fixed something and the ceiling should be lowered in that same commit, not silently absorbed.

voterJest.reason: This phase (the authority web dashboard) touches nothing in apps/VoteTorrentVoter. Importing an unrelated red baseline into a gate whose whole value is trustworthiness would make the gate less useful, not more. Recorded here, and echoed to every CI run's job summary, precisely so it cannot be silently forgotten -- it is not this phase's to fix, and it is not this workflow's to run.
